subject: Biology
title: Herd Immunity
description: A fast breakdown of Herd Immunity for builders.

hook.text: When enough people are immune, a disease can't spread—even to those who aren't vaccinated.

buildup.text: Herd immunity occurs when 80–95% of a population is immune, depending on the disease.

discovery.text: The virus runs out of susceptible hosts. Transmission chains break and the outbreak dies out.

twist.text: Herd immunity protects babies, elderly, and immunocompromised people who can't be vaccinated.

climax.text: When vaccination rates drop, herd immunity breaks—and diseases like measles return.

punchline.text: Your immunity protects your neighbor. Their immunity protects you.

quiz.question: Who benefits most from herd immunity?

details.summary: Herd immunity occurs when enough individuals in a population are immune to a disease that it cannot spread effectively, protecting even unvaccinated members. The threshold varies by disease: measles requires about 95 percent immunity, while polio needs around 80 percent.
details.whyItMatters: Herd immunity is the foundation of public health vaccination strategy. It protects vulnerable people who cannot be vaccinated, such as infants and immunocompromised individuals, and is the mechanism by which diseases like smallpox were eradicated.
takeaways: Herd immunity protects unvaccinated individuals through community-wide coverage
Highly contagious diseases like measles require 95 percent immunity threshold
Herd immunity enabled the eradication of smallpox and near-elimination of polio

faq.question: Why does measles require such a high vaccination rate for herd immunity?
faq.answer: Measles is extremely contagious, with one infected person spreading it to 12 to 18 others on average. To stop transmission, nearly everyone must be immune so the virus cannot find enough susceptible hosts. Even small drops in vaccination rates cause outbreaks.

faq.question: Can herd immunity be achieved through natural infection alone?
faq.answer: Theoretically yes, but the cost in severe illness and death would be enormous. For COVID-19, natural herd immunity would have required hundreds of millions of infections. Vaccines achieve the same community protection with dramatically less suffering.
